title: harmonize-resume-token-and-retry-semantics-across-sdks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We have three orthogonal but related inconsistencies across the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that cause integration pain for customers and downstream services: (1) the streaming continuation token is exposed with different names and shapes (cursor / resume_token / continuation) and inconsistent encoding, (2) retry semantics for transient streaming failures are underspecified and diverge between languages (how idempotency, retry window, and max_attempts are expressed), and (3) streaming telemetry (trace IDs and per-chunk stream IDs) are not consistently propagated which complicates correlating client-side retries with server-side logs.

What this PR does: Consolidates naming and runtime behavior across SDKs with a minimal compatibility surface. High-level changes included in this single PR: add a stable resumeToken field (camelCase) exposed by all three SDKs with a migration shim for legacy names; define a small, explicit RetryProfile contract and default presets (fast, steady, conservative) implemented in each SDK; standardize the retry-window parameter name to retryWindowMs (milliseconds) and the maxAttempts param to maxAttempts; wire a stream-scoped telemetry header (X-Redwood-Stream-Id) and ensure the SDKs attach the trace_id to streaming chunks for server-side trace joins; bump library versions to reflect the changes and ship compatibility adapters.

Why in one PR: This change touches behavior across runtime boundaries and we wanted to guarantee parity in a single coordinated rollout to avoid split-brain UX for downstream SDK consumers. The core of the change is language-agnostic: a small surface contract (resumeToken + RetryProfile + telemetry headers) and per-language adapters that implement that contract idiomatically.

Checklist:
- [x] Define canonical field name and encoding for resume tokens and add migration shims in each SDK
- [x] Implement RetryProfile primitives and three default presets in Python/TS/Go
- [x] Add unit and integration tests (local stream replay + server-side correlation test)
- [x] Attach X-Redwood-Stream-Id and trace_id to stream chunks where available
- [x] Update CHANGELOGs and bump package versions (py: 0.14.2 -> 0.15.0, ts: 2.3.0 -> 2.4.0, go: v1.11.0 -> v1.12.0)
- [x] Add migration note to SDK docs and an example for converting legacy cursor payloads

Description of notable changes (single-line summaries):
- SDK: Introduce resumeToken canonicalization and migration helpers (sdk/python, sdk/typescript, sdk/go)
- SDK: Add RetryProfile object + defaultProfiles and expose from public surface
- SDK: Normalize retryWindowMs and maxAttempts param names and validation rules
- SDK: Stream telemetry: X-Redwood-Stream-Id header + attach trace_id to chunk envelopes when present
- Docs: Migration guide + examples and CHANGELOG entries for all three SDKs
- Tests: end-to-end streaming replay tests that assert token resumption + telemetry correlation

Notes on compatibility: The resumeToken property is additive; shims accept previous names (cursor, continuation) and will emit resumeToken in new responses. The RetryProfile defaults were chosen to approximate existing behavior (fast ~ previous short backoff, steady ~ current default, conservative ~ backing off longer for unstable networks). No breaking API surface is removed; the PR is marked as non-breaking but requires coordinated language bumps to get the consistent semantics in client applications.

release_notes:
- SDKs: Add resumeToken canonical field and migration shims across Python/TypeScript/Go.
- SDKs: Introduce RetryProfile + default presets (fast/steady/conservative) and standardize retryWindowMs and maxAttempts.
- Streaming: Attach X-Redwood-Stream-Id header and propagate trace_id into chunk envelopes for better correlation.
- Examples and migration guide added.
- Version bumps: python 0.15.0, typescript 2.4.0, go v1.12.0.
